title: Serving features online and offline
prompt: Your model trains on historical features in batch and needs the same features served at inference. How do you store and serve features so training and serving agree?
constraint: Eliminate train/serve skew (identical feature values at training and inference) while keeping online serving latency low (single-digit ms).

options.why: One feature-definition pipeline computes values once and materializes them to both a low-latency online KV store (serving) and an offline columnar store (training). Identical computation feeds both, so values match — killing skew — while the online store delivers single-digit-ms reads. Best fit for the constraint.

Computing at request time from raw data can guarantee training/serving use the same code path, removing skew. Defensible, but heavy aggregations over historical windows blow the latency budget unless features are trivial — weaker under the low-latency constraint.

A single backend can't be both: an OLAP/columnar store can't hit single-digit-ms point lookups, and a KV store can't do efficient large-scale historical scans for training. You'd violate either the latency or the training-access need — not a fit.

Online stores hold only current/recent values, not the full point-in-time history training needs. Reconstructing past feature values from live state reintroduces leakage and skew — the exact thing the constraint forbids.
